title: HPLC and LC–MS/MS analysis of intermediate wheatgrass protein composition
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

Intermediate wheatgrass (IWG) has emerged as a grain of interest due to its perennial nature and its ecological benefits. However, significant differences in functionality between IWG and hexaploid bread wheat are present and uptake of IWG in the market has been low, primarily due to difficulties in utilization. Differences in functionality relate primarily to the presence or absence of specific gluten forming proteins.

RESULTS

IWG has gliadins in a similar banding pattern and molecular weight range compared to traditional wheat as per sodium dodecyl sulfate–polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE) analysis. However, there are significant differences in high-molecular-weight glutenin (HMWG), which is primarily responsible for protein–protein interactions and elasticity of the gluten network. The molecular weight distribution of IWG specifically has a lower HMWG unextractable fraction compared to traditional wheat, which is a key indicator of a flour with a strong gluten network. Lastly, when identifying specific HMWG proteins, there were some similar compounds, however, the concentrations were different. IWG was notably lacking in HMWG subunits DY10 and DX5.

CONCLUSION

The significant differences in protein composition and molecular weight distribution provide insight into the challenges IWG faces while trying to be adopted into mainstream production. This study helps contribute to the growing body of research which will aid in focusing breeding efforts on specific gluten forming proteins and improving the functionality of IWG gluten forming proteins and therefore its marketability. © 2026 The Author(s).
